'''Erika Lee McEntarfer''' (born January 1973) is an American labor economist who served as the [[Commissioner of Labor Statistics|commissioner of labor statistics]] from 2024 to 2025.

McEntarfer graduated from [[Bard College]] with a bachelor's degree in social science and from [[Virginia Tech]] with a doctorate in economics. She worked in the [[United States Department of the Treasury]]'s [[Office of Tax Policy]] before becoming an economist in the [[United States Census Bureau|Census Bureau]]'s [[Center for Economic Studies (U.S. Census Bureau)|Center for Economic Studies]]. In the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]], McEntarfer was a senior economist in the [[Council of Economic Advisers]]. 

In July 2023, President [[Joe Biden]] nominated McEntarfer to serve as Commissioner of Labor Statistics at the [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]]. She was confirmed by the [[United States Senate|Senate]] in January 2024. On August 1, 2025, President [[Donald Trump]] controversially fired McEntarfer as commissioner, hours after a weak jobs report from the Bureau. Without evidence, Trump said McEntarfer had manipulated the jobs numbers, an allegation dismissed by economists. The firing was condemned by economists who saw it as politicizing national statistics and undermining trustworthiness of government data produced under the Trump administration. A 2026 NBER paper estimated that Trump's firing of McEntarfer cost the US economy $20 billion by creating economic policy uncertainty and undermining trust in official statistics, altering behaviors by investors, businesses, and households.<ref name=":1">{{Citation |last=Bloom |first=Nicholas |title=The Value of Reliable Statistics |date=2026 |type=Working Paper |url=https://www.nber.org/papers/w35135 |series=Working Paper Series |publisher=National Bureau of Economic Research |doi=10.3386/w35135 |id=35135 |last2=Groshen |first2=Erica L. |last3=Hobbs |first3=Duncan |last4=Strain |first4=Michael R.}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
McEntarfer was born in January 1973.<ref>{{Cite document |title=Erika L McEntarfer in the U.S., Index to Public Records, 1994–2019 |publisher=Index to Public Records}}</ref> She graduated from [[Bard College]] with a bachelor's degree in social science and from [[Virginia Tech]] with a PhD in economics.<ref name="TheHillInfo">{{Cite web |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5432920-bls-commisioner-eirka-mcentarfer-trump-firing/ |title=Who is Erika McEntarfer, labor statistics chief sacked by Trump |date=August 1, 2025 |last=Timotija |first=Filip |work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] |access-date=August 1, 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
===Early work in the Federal government===
From 2002–2008, McEntarfer worked as an economist at the Census Bureau's Longitudinal Employer–Household Dynamics Program; from 2018–2019 she was head of research for the  program.<ref name="CV" /><ref name="BLS" /> From 2010, she was a lead Labor Markets economist in the [[United States Census Bureau|Census Bureau]]'s [[Center for Economic Studies (U.S. Census Bureau)|Center for Economic Studies]].<ref name="CV" /><ref name="BloombergLawConfirmed">{{Cite web |url=https://news.bloomberglaw.com/daily-labor-report/senate-confirms-biden-pick-to-lead-bureau-of-labor-statistics |title=Senate Confirms Biden Pick to Lead Bureau of Labor Statistics |date=January 11, 2024 |last=Munhoz |first=Diego |publisher=[[Bloomberg Law]] |access-date=August 1, 2025}}</ref> In periods when she was away from the Census Bureau, McEntarfer had been on the economic staff of the Treasury Department's [[Office of Tax Policy]] in 2008–2010, and immediately before her appointment to the BLS had been on the nonpolitical staff of the White House [[Council of Economic Advisers]] for a year.<ref name="CV">{{cite web |title=ERIKA McENTARFER, Ph.D. |url=https://erikamcentarfer.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/cv-mcentarfer.pdf |access-date=August 2, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241005183811/https://erikamcentarfer.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/cv-mcentarfer.pdf |archive-date=October 5, 2024 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="BLS">[https://www.bls.gov/bls/senior_staff/mcentarfer.htm Dr. Erika McEntarfer, Commissioner], official page at BLS</ref><ref name="TheHillInfo"/>

===Commissioner of Labor Statistics (2024–2025)===
In July 2023, President [[Joe Biden]] nominated McEntarfer to serve as [[Commissioner of Labor Statistics]] at the [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]] (BLS). She was confirmed by the [[United States Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions|Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions]] in October 2023,<ref name="BloombergLawConfirmed"/> and by the full [[United States Senate]] on an 86–8 vote in January 2024.<ref name="BloombergFiring">{{Cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Molly |last2=Woodhouse |first2=Skylar |date=August 1, 2025 |title=Trump Moves to Fire Labor Statistics Head After Weak Jobs Data |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-08-01/trump-says-he-ll-fire-labor-statistics-head-after-weak-jobs-data |access-date=August 1, 2025 |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |publisher=}}</ref> 

As commissioner, McEntarfer moved to reduce the sample size of the household survey in the monthly jobs report by five thousand households due to budget constraints.<ref name="tanzi">{{Cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-06-07/us-jobs-household-survey-size-to-be-cut-amid-budget-constraints |title=US Jobs Household Survey Size to Be Cut Due to Budget Constraints |date=June 7, 2024 |last=Tanzi |first=Alexandre |publisher=[[Bloomberg News]] |access-date=August 1, 2025}}</ref> After the [[United States Department of Labor|Department of Labor]] determined{{when|date=August 2025}} that the Bureau of Labor Statistics was "not sufficiently focused" on its process to disseminate sensitive economic information, she led the Bureau's response to follow the department's review.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Saraiva |first=Augusta |date=December 10, 2024 |title=BLS Needs Culture Revamp After Botched US Releases, Review Finds |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-12-10/bls-needs-culture-revamp-after-botched-us-releases-review-finds |access-date=August 1, 2025 |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |publisher=}}</ref>

====Firing by Donald Trump====
{{See also|False or misleading statements by Donald Trump#Firing of Erika McEntarfer|Bureau of Labor Statistics#Firing of Commissioner McEntarfer}}
[[File:2021- Change in non-farm employment - US.svg |thumb |Trump fired McEntarfer soon after a downward revision to the July 2025 employment statistic, but subsequent months showed no net improvement over July's number.<ref name=BLS_EmploymentChange_20251228>{{cite web |title=Top Picks / Employment, Hours, and Earnings from the Current Employment Statistics survey (National) |url=https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/CES0000000001 |publisher=US Bureau of Labor Statistics |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251229013219/https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/CES0000000001 |archive-date=29 December 2025 |date=28 December 2025 |url-status=live}} Click "More formatting options" and choose "1-Month Net Change". — Can access via [https://data.bls.gov/toppicks?survey=ce "Top Picks" list], select "Total Nonfarm Employment, Seasonally Adjusted - CES0000000001" and click "Retrieve data" button. Then click "More formatting options" and choose "1-Month Net Change".</ref>]]
On August 1, 2025, President [[Donald Trump]] announced that he had directed his staff to fire McEntarfer, hours after the Bureau's July jobs report, which included a substantial downward revision of reported job creation from the prior two months and weaker-than-expected job creation for July.<ref name="tanzi"/><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/trump-orders-firing-of-bureau-of-labor-statistics-chief-d8eaa272 |title=Trump Orders Firing of Bureau of Labor Statistics Chief |date=August 1, 2025 |last1=Lahart |first1=Justin |last2=Leary |first2=Alex |last3=Grossman |first3=Matt |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |access-date=August 1, 2025}}</ref> In a post on [[Truth Social]], Trump accused McEntarfer, without evidence (according to the ''[[Financial Times]]''), of incompetence and of having an ulterior motive for allegedly altering employment figures in order to discredit him and Republicans, and to help Democratic nominee [[Kamala Harris]] in the [[2024 United States presidential election]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ft.com/content/023b5ad5-b946-486d-a55f-36a9a9f62443 |title=Donald Trump to fire US labour statistics boss after weak jobs report |date=August 1, 2025 |last1=McCormick |first1=Myles |last2=Jones |first2=Claire |last3=Steer |first3=George |work=[[Financial Times]] |quote= '[McEntarfer] will be replaced with someone much more competent and qualified. Important numbers like this ... can’t be manipulated for political purposes,' Trump said, claiming without evidence that she had massaged figures to help the former president ... The president alleged that the data had been 'RIGGED in order to make the Republicans, and ME, look bad' |access-date=August 1, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Sheth |first1=Sonam |last2=Whisnant |first2=Gabe |date=August 1, 2025 |title=Donald Trump Fires Person Behind Jobs Numbers After They're Revised Down |url=https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-job-numbers-revised-down-fires-appointee-2107768 |access-date=August 2, 2025 |work=[[Newsweek]] |pages= |quote='Dr. Erika McEntarfer ... faked the Jobs Numbers before the Election to try and boost Kamala's chances of Victory,' Trump posted on Truth Social, referring to former Democratic presidential nominee Kamala Harris. |agency=}}</ref> McEntarfer received notice of her firing hours later.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/live/2025/07/31/business/tariffs-trump-trade/234cd5c1-32c0-5f3b-abe0-a977e1d6f343 |title=The commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics, Erika McEntarfer, has been officially fired and informed of her firing, according to a person familiar with the matter who declined to be named. |date=August 1, 2025 |last=Ember |first=Sydney |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=August 1, 2025}}</ref>

Trump's assertion that McEntarfer had manipulated the jobs numbers was without evidence and dismissed by economists.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Kiernan |first=Paul |date=2025 |title=What Happens When Politicians Meddle With Economic Data: Argentina's Example |url=https://www.wsj.com/economy/trump-jobs-economic-data-risk-e4b7410b |website=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US}}</ref>

==== Criticism of firing ====
The firing drew widespread criticism from former and current economists,<ref name="BBC1">{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvg3xrrzdr0o |title=Trump fires lead official on economic data as tariffs cause market drop |date=August 2, 2025 |last1=Sherman |first1=Natalie |work=[[BBC]] |access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2025/08/02/trump-economic-uncertainty/ |title=Economic fears of investors are here — and fed by Trump's reaction |date=August 2, 2025 |last1=Lynch |first1=David |last2=Bhattarai |first2=Abha |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/larry-summers-trumps-accusations-manipulated-jobs-numbers-preposterous/story?id=124321470|title=Larry Summers says Trump's accusations of manipulated jobs numbers are 'preposterous' |date=August 3, 2025 |last1=Kerr |first1=Nicholas |work=ABC News |access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref> including McEntarfer's predecessor as BLS commissioner, economist [[William Beach (economist)|William Beach]], who called the firing "totally groundless". According to economists, the firing of statisticians for publishing inconvenient data and replacing them with loyalists who might manipulate data served to politicize national statistics and undermine their trustworthiness, which would have adverse economic consequences.<ref name=":0" /> In an interview with [[Kasie Hunt]] on the Sunday talk show ''[[State of the Union (American TV program)|State of the Union]]'', Beach said:<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-03 |title=Former Trump statistics chief slams Friday firing of Erika McEntarfer |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/08/03/trump-labor-statistics-chief-fired-unemployment-00490988 |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=POLITICO|last=Svirnovskiy|first=Gregory}}</ref><blockquote>The commissioner doesn't do anything to collect the numbers. The commissioner doesn't see the numbers for until Wednesday before they're published. By the time the commissioner sees the numbers, they're all prepared.</blockquote>[[Jed Kolko]], a senior fellow at the [[Peterson Institute for International Economics]], said the firing was a "five-alarm intentional harm to the integrity of US economic data and the entire statistical system."<ref name="BBC1" /> In an editorial, ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' commented that "Mr. Trump's data denial is one more reason fewer Americans will trust the government."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.wsj.com/opinion/the-bureau-of-labor-denial-851be8c0?gaa_at=eafs&gaa_n=ASWzDAjsyplIm3sfFVB1u5-WOHJUthZe5_lFKBduVjqBT6dIh7UlgAwyhbubBvHABs4%3D&gaa_ts=688fd21a&gaa_sig=dt6IJa4pNTRTlBsWp1bUgRlnjVL5wC2gOgSpGMbhmAIC3se2d7wf5HhCU9zJ6KFsOUhnveKeV4kjPXgTG6-CUw%3D%3D|title=The Bureau of Labor Denial |date=August 3, 2025 |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref> Commentators pointed out that, with BLS security precautions, the commissioner does not have access to the systems that collect the data for these reports and could not alter the results without a large number of people knowing and possibly complaining publicly.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/08/04/nx-s1-5490075/a-former-bureau-of-labor-statistics-commissioner-on-the-firing-of-bls-head |title=A former Bureau of Labor Statistics commissioner on the firing of BLS head |date=August 4, 2025 |publisher=[[NPR]] |author=Leila Fadel }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Aratani |first=Lauren |title=Labor statistics chief fired by Trump sounds alarm over White House’s ‘dangerous’ interference |publisher=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2025/sep/17/labor-statistics-chief-trump-erika-mcentarfer |date=2025-09-17 |access-date=2025-12-28}}</ref> A 2026 NBER paper estimated that McEntarfer's firing harmed the US economy to the tune of approximately $20 billion by introducing economic policy uncertainty and undermining the integrity and quality of official statistics, leading to shifting behaviors by investors, households, and businesses.<ref name=":1" /> McEntarfer herself stated that BLS data should still be trusted even despite her firing, as the same agency staff were still running the bureau and are "blowing a loud whistle if there is interference."<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-02-11 |title=Erika McEntarfer (@erikamcentarfer.bsky.social) |url=https://bsky.app/profile/erikamcentarfer.bsky.social/post/3melvdmr56k2n |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20260211221101/https://bsky.app/profile/erikamcentarfer.bsky.social/post/3melvdmr56k2n |archive-date=2026-02-11 |access-date=2026-07-22 |work=Bluesky Social}}</ref>

==== New nominee for commissioner of labor of statistics position ====
{{Coatrack|section|date=July 2026}}
The Bureau's deputy commissioner, [[William Wiatrowski]], was named as McEntarfer's acting successor.<ref name="BloombergFiring"/> On August 11, Trump nominated [[E.J. Antoni]] to replace McEntarfer as commissioner.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rugaber |first1=Christopher |title=Trump nominates conservative economist to head agency that compiles jobs, inflation data |url=https://apnews.com/article/trump-jobs-inflation-labor-statistics-antoni-ee8ed2b08369d9e292a70f326db0f423 |access-date=August 16, 2025 |work=[[Associated Press News]] |date=August 11, 2025}}</ref> In contrast to McEntarfer, Antoni had no experience in government, no substantive academic work, and a track record of echoing Trump rhetoric and lauding Trump, including having a since-deleted homophobic and misogynist Twitter account.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaczynski |first=Andrew |last2=Steck |first2=Em |date=2025-09-05 |title=Trump's pick to lead Bureau of Labor Statistics ran anonymous Twitter account filled with sexually degrading and bigoted attacks {{!}} CNN Politics |url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/09/05/politics/kfile-ej-antoni-bureau-of-labor-statistics-twitter-account-vis |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Gilbert |first=David |date=2025 |title=An Account Using the Same Name as Trump's BLS Pick Posted Red-Pilled Conspiracy Theories |url=https://www.wired.com/story/twitter-ej-antoni-trump-bls-conspiracy-theories-epstein-covid-election-denial/ |access-date=2025-09-05 |magazine=Wired |language=en-US |issn=1059-1028}}</ref> After criticism of Antoni's nomination and Twitter account, Trump withdrew the nomination in September.<ref name="CNN-nomination-withdrawn">{{cite web |last1=Homes |first1=Kristen |last2=Cancryn |first2=Adam |last3=Kaczynski |first3=Andrew |title=White House withdraws Trump’s controversial nominee to lead BLS after ousting predecessor over jobs data |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2025/09/30/politics/ej-antoni-nomination-withdrawn-bls |website=CNN |access-date=4 October 2025 |date=30 September 2025}}</ref> Wiatrowski continued to serve as interim commissioner as of February 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bls.gov/bls/senior_staff/wiatrowski.htm|title=William J. Wiatrowski, Deputy Commissioner|website=Bureau of Labor Statistics}}</ref> 

==Post‑government career==
Following her dismissal as Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics in August 2025, McEntarfer joined the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research as a Research Scholar and Distinguished Policy Fellow, focusing on labor economics, economic policy, and the interpretation of government data.<ref>{{cite web |title=Current Policy Fellows |url=https://siepr.stanford.edu/people/policy-fellow/current-policy-fellows |publisher=Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research |access-date=2025-12-28}}</ref>

She has delivered public lectures and participated in academic events emphasizing the importance of independent and credible economic statistics, including talks at her alma mater, Bard College, on the role of official data in evaluating economic conditions.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Importance of Official Data in Assessing Economic Conditions |url=https://www.bard.edu/news/events/the-importance-of-official-data-in-assessing-economic-conditions |publisher=Bard College |access-date=2025-12-28}}</ref>

McEntarfer has also provided commentary in the media on the risks of politicizing labor statistics and the need to maintain the integrity of federal statistical agencies, warning that interference in data reporting could undermine public trust in economic information.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ex-BLS chief says her firing marked 'dangerous step' for economy |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/ex-bls-chief-says-her-firing-by-trump-marked-dangerous-step-economy-2025-09-16/ |publisher=Reuters |access-date=2025-12-28}}</ref>
